linked_issues.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Adding a no-op `mode='before'` model validator makes smart-union validation select a model with fewer matching fields for JSON input. The equivalent Python input selects the model with more matching fields.

The example below prints:

```text
Larger
Smaller
```

I expect `Larger` in both cases: it has three supplied valid fields, while `Smaller` has two. This follows the documented [number-of-valid-fields-set ranking](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/unions/#number-of-valid-fields-set).

Reproduced on `main` at 965c23dd93bd5ca7b86224ba39ccbe79399f117b. In [model_fields.rs](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/965c23dd93bd5ca7b86224ba39ccbe79399f117b/pydantic-core/src/validators/model_fields.rs), the Python-input helper adds its known-field count, then the outer validator adds `fields_set.len()` again. The before validator sends the smaller model through that Python-input path, while the larger model uses the plain JSON path and receives only the outer count.

I can send a focused fix with regression tests. Could you assign this to me?

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, TypeAdapter, model_validator


class Smaller(BaseModel):
    a: int
    b: int

    @model_validator(mode='before')
    @classmethod
    def keep_input(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        return value


class Larger(BaseModel):
    a: int
    b: int
    c: int

packet.body_excerpt:
## Change Summary

A model before validator converts JSON input to Python values. The Python-input helper counted supplied fields, then the outer validator counted them again. This let a smaller union member with a before validator outrank a larger member using the plain JSON path.

Count successfully validated, explicitly supplied known fields once in each input-specific helper. Preserve nested counts without counting extra keys or defaults as local fields.

The regression covers Python and JSON input, both union orders, and ignored or allowed extras.

Edit by @Viicos: this also does not count extra fields anymore, this was most likely a regression too and doesn't really make sense. 

## Related issue number

Fixes #13729.
